name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
summary: A foundational breathwork drill performed supine to promote deep diaphragmatic expansion and down-regulate the nervous system.

setup: Lie comfortably on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, or with legs extended over a bolster.
Place one hand on your upper chest and the other hand on your abdomen just below the ribcage.
Relax your shoulders, neck, and jaw, maintaining a neutral spine.
steps: Inhale slowly through your nose, directing the air deep into your abdomen so that the hand on your belly rises while the hand on your chest stays relatively still.
Pause briefly at the top of the inhalation without straining.
Exhale slowly and smoothly through pursed lips or your nose, feeling the hand on your abdomen gently fall as your belly relaxes inward.
instructions.breathing: Inhale deeply into the abdomen for three to four seconds, pause briefly, and exhale smoothly for four to six seconds.
cues: Breathe into your stomach, not your shoulders
Keep the chest still and neck relaxed

common_faults.fault: Chest and shoulder elevation during inhalation.
common_faults.correction: Focus on keeping the upper hand still while guiding movement into the lower hand on your abdomen.

common_faults.fault: Forcefully pushing the abdominal wall out rather than letting incoming air expand it naturally.
common_faults.correction: Inhale gently and smoothly, allowing the diaphragm to naturally expand the belly.

precautions: If you feel lightheaded, return to normal tidal breathing and rest.
